lyrics:
[Verse 1: a cappella, solo female voice, no instruments at all]
There's a bag beside the doorway
There's a note beside the bed
I have loved you past the saying
So I'll leave the rest unsaid

[Chorus: still a cappella, soft, a single held note]
I'm leaving you the light on
I'm leaving you the key
I'm leaving you the best years
That you ever gave to me
I'm leaving you the light

[Verse 2: soft electric piano, bass and brushes enter]
Take the laughing, take the summers
Take the kitchen and the songs
I am taking only this much:
That I loved you all along

[Chorus: fuller, strings join, voice opens up]
I'm leaving you the light on
I'm leaving you the key
I'm leaving you the best years
That you ever gave to me
I'm leaving you the light

[Saxophone Solo: tenor sax plays the chorus melody, tender]

[Verse 3: quiet, almost spoken, a blessing]
May the mornings treat you gently
May your table stay full
May somebody learn to hold you
In the way I never could

[Break: everything stops, silence, one huge drum hit]

[Final Chorus: key change up, full power, long held notes]
I'm leaving you the light on
I'm leaving you the key
I'm leaving you the best years
That you ever gave to me
I'm leaving you the light
Oh, I'm leaving you the light

[Outro: band fades, voice alone again, very soft]
The light
I'm leaving you
Tonight
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 66 BPM, 4/4, A major, rising to B major after the break. Very slow and still, then overwhelming.

VOICE: Female soprano with enormous range and control. The first verse and chorus are sung with no accompaniment, soft and breathy with small gospel turns. Each chorus is fuller than the last. After the key change she sings at full power with long held notes and melismatic runs, then returns to a whisper.

INSTRUMENTS: Nothing for the first 50 seconds. Then soft electric piano, fretless bass and brushed drums. A string section that grows from one line to a full orchestra. A tenor saxophone for one solo. A single, very large tom and bass-drum hit that marks the key change. Acoustic guitar picking under verse 3.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Verse 1 and chorus, voice entirely alone. 0:52 Verse 2, the band enters gently. 1:18 Chorus 2, strings. 1:50 Saxophone solo on the chorus tune. 2:16 Verse 3, quiet, a blessing. 2:44 Break: everything stops for a full bar of silence, then one drum hit. 2:48 Final chorus in the new key, at full power, with the last line repeated. 3:36 Outro, the band fades and the voice ends alone at 4:10.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-90s adult-pop ballad production: lush, wide and reverberant, with the voice far in front of everything and plenty of dynamic range.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The silence and single drum hit at 2:44, and the first held note after it.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The lyric is written so that the leaving need not be a break-up. It is equally a parent, a mentor or someone at the end of a life, which is how older listeners will hear it.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Stillness, grace, grief held in check, then released.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Someone is leaving in the night, out of love, and leaves a light on behind her.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: the end of a marriage with no villain; a mother seeing a child off to a new life; a dying parent; a mentor retiring. The key line is heard two ways and the outro confirms both.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: an unaccompanied opening, a blameless goodbye, a blessing verse, a full stop with one drum hit, then a key change and a long held note. Designed mishearing: 'I'm leaving you the light on' is heard as 'I'm leaving you tonight', which is also true.
